name: FSRS spaced-repetition scheduler
rule: Each atom has one card with stability S and difficulty D. Retrievability is R(t,S) = (1 + FACTOR*t/S)^DECAY; the next interval is the day count at which R falls to the target retention, rounded, floored at 1 day and capped. A rating of 1 sets the card to relearning with a 1-day interval and takes the forget-stability formula; ratings 2 to 4 take the recall-stability formula.

parameters.name: weights w0..w18
parameters.source: no stated source for the 19 values; the constant is named FSRS_DEFAULT_W and docs call the scheduler FSRS-5

parameters.name: DECAY
parameters.source: KNOWLEDGE-ENGINEERING.md section 1.3 (FSRS-5: FACTOR 19/81, DECAY 0.5), citing Expertium and the awesome-fsrs wiki

parameters.name: requestRetention
parameters.source: DECISIONS.md decision 3 (target retention 0.90); PRODUCT-LANDSCAPE.md case study 4 cites faqs.ankiweb.net for Anki's 90% default

internal_sources.line_or_heading: 1.3 The FSRS memory model, made precise

measured_by: Web Learn stores engine state per branch: per atom stability, difficulty, due, lastReview, reps, lapses, firedCredit, theta, n, plus xp, streak and per-day counts of new and reviewed atoms (src/lib/academy/mastery.ts StoredEngineState). No per-review row is kept on the web. bkt local: attempts table (item_id, mode, encrypted response, correct, rating, elapsed_ms, at) and an outbox row per attempt (packages/bkt/src/store.ts lines 95-99, 363-374). Predicted R is never compared with a later observed recall.
verification: doc-and-code-disagree: DECISIONS.md decision 3 says FSRS-6 through the ts-fsrs library with a py-fsrs optimizer; the code is a hand-written FSRS-5 class with fixed weights and no optimizer. Weights w17 and w18 are never read in fsrs.ts.
notes: Lean proves the clamps and interval bounds only; docs/ARCHITECTURE-TARGET.md says schedule values stay unverified because they pass through exp and pow. That doc also records a bug: stored stability at or below 0 gives NaN.

name: Mastery from stability alone
rule: When an atom has a card but no proficiency attempts, mastery = 1 - exp(-S/21), clamped to 0..1.
measured_by: Derived from stored stability; nothing checks it against outcomes.

name: Elo-style proficiency per atom
rule: Each graded attempt updates theta: P = sigmoid(slope*(theta - b_depth)), K = a/(1 + b*n), theta += K*(score - P), n += 1. The score comes from the 1-4 rating. Depth difficulty b is a fixed table; item difficulty is never updated.

parameters.name: PROF_K_A
parameters.source: ADAPTIVE-SOTA.md b.1: U(n)=a/(1+b*n) with a=1, b=0.05, citing Pelánek 2016

cited_works.title: Applications of the Elo Rating System in Adaptive Educational Systems

measured_by: theta and n are stored per atom (web state; bkt learn_prof table). No calibration check of P against observed correctness.
verification: doc-and-code-disagree: ADAPTIVE-SOTA.md b.1 updates item difficulty b too and b.3 evaluates P at the lower bound of the theta confidence interval against an Angoff cut; the code keeps a fixed four-row depth table and uses the point estimate at b = -0.2.
notes: Self-ratings feed theta, so self-report raises mastery; ADAPTIVE-SOTA.md c.3 says self-report should affect scheduling only.

name: Mastery formula M = P^alpha * R^beta
rule: With at least one proficiency attempt, P = sigmoid(theta - b_apply), R = FSRS retrievability at a fixed horizon, and M = P^alpha * R^beta, zero if either is zero. An atom counts as mastered at M >= 0.7.

parameters.name: MASTERY_ALPHA
parameters.source: ADAPTIVE-SOTA.md b.3 (start alpha = beta = 1); the doc calls the formula its own synthesis with no paper behind it

parameters.name: RETENTION_HORIZON_DAYS
parameters.source: ADAPTIVE-SOTA.md b.3 gives 90 days as an example; no citation

internal_sources.line_or_heading: b.3 The fusion formula; gaps / kill-criteria item 1

measured_by: M, P and R are computed on read from stored state. No retest at the 90-day horizon exists, and M is not compared with any exam result.
verification: doc-and-code-disagree: DECISIONS.md decision 11 sets mastery as BKT fused with FSRS at P >= 0.95; the code uses Elo with M >= 0.7. ADAPTIVE-SOTA.md adds per-concept Angoff cuts and a conjunctive overall gate that the code lacks.
notes: EPIC.md and ADAPTIVE-SOTA.md both say the formula is unvalidated and must be checked against real exam performance before a public rating ships. The public profile carries a disclaimer that it is no certified score (src/lib/academy/profile.ts lines 91-94).

name: Question depth picked from mastery
rule: Each atom has quiz items at up to four levels. The level asked is recall below M 0.25, apply below 0.5, derive below 0.75, teach above, falling back to the nearest lower level the atom has.

parameters.name: levels
parameters.source: DECISIONS.md decision 3 names the four mastery signals; no paper cited

measured_by: The level of each graded item is in the assess_done event and in the bkt items table; no outcome is tied to level.

name: Two-layer graph: prerequisite edges plus encompassing weights
rule: Layer one is the authored requires list. Layer two is computed: every prerequisite within 4 hops gets weight 0.6 * 0.5^(hops-1), dropped below 0.05.

cited_works.title: How Math Academy Creates its Knowledge Graph
Optimized, Individualized Spaced Repetition in Hierarchical Knowledge Structures

measured_by: nothing
verification: doc-and-code-disagree: ADAPTIVE-SOTA.md a.1 describes expert-set weights in an encompasses block on each atom, each meaning the share of the simpler skill a harder problem exercises; the code derives every weight from hop distance and reads no authored weight.
notes: ADAPTIVE-SOTA.md gap 2 says encompassing weights are untested outside math.

name: FIRe: implicit review credit to prerequisites
rule: On a rating of 3 or 4, each encompassed prerequisite with a card and retrievability at or above 0.6 gets credit = min(0.5, weight*0.5) * ratingScore; its stability grows by min(0.15, credit*0.15) and its due date moves later, never earlier. No penalty travels to dependents on a miss.

cited_works.title: Optimized, Individualized Spaced Repetition in Hierarchical Knowledge Structures
How Our AI Works

measured_by: firedCredit accumulates on each credited card. Nothing records whether a credited atom was later recalled.
verification: doc-and-code-disagree: PRODUCT-LANDSCAPE.md describes FIRe as credit down and penalties up; the code sends credit down only.
notes: Largest stability gain per event is 0.6*0.5*0.15 = 4.5 percent for a direct prerequisite.

name: Leverage of an atom
rule: leverage = (count of transitive dependents + 0.5 * direct dependents) / the largest such value in the deck.

internal_sources.line_or_heading: e.2 The four measures + Borda aggregation

measured_by: nothing
verification: doc-and-code-disagree: DECISIONS.md decision 9 defines the Reach Score as PageRank 0.45, reach 0.30, betweenness 0.15, k-core 0.10, and ADAPTIVE-SOTA.md e.2 replaces that with Borda aggregation; the code uses dependents counts alone.

name: Daily route: due reviews then new atoms
rule: The route lists every card due now, oldest first, then up to newPerDay new atoms minus those already introduced today. A new atom is eligible when every prerequisite has a card; eligible atoms sort by shell (prereq, nucleus, frontier) then leverage.

parameters.name: unlock rule
parameters.value: each prerequisite has a card, regardless of its mastery

parameters.name: shell order
parameters.source: DECISIONS.md Convergence 2 (reach-weighted walk over the outer fringe)

measured_by: Per-day counts of new and reviewed atoms; study_session_done carries items, correct and seconds. Events placement_done, study_session_done, assess_done, tutor_turn (src/lib/academy/events.ts), recorded only for an 18plus profile with learn_event consent (events-server.ts lines 30-35).
verification: doc-and-code-disagree: ADAPTIVE-SOTA.md a.4 opens an atom when its prerequisites are mastered; the code opens it when they have been seen once. LITERATURE-REVIEW.md asks the session builder to mix atoms across branches; route() works inside one branch.

name: Path to a target topic
rule: For a chosen target the planner takes the prerequisite closure, orders it topologically with a rank tie-break, and returns the atoms not yet mastered as steps. It fails on a missing node, a cycle, or a mastered atom whose prerequisite is unmastered; repairMastery demotes such atoms.
measured_by: nothing
notes: The Lean theorems are about an abstract edge relation; I found no check that binds them to prereq-path.ts.

name: Topic map with four states
rule: Each topic shows as known (has a card), due (card due now), new (every prerequisite has a card) or locked. Columns are prerequisite depth, left to right.
measured_by: nothing
notes: Known means studied once, a weaker test than mastered.

name: Adaptive placement
rule: Each atom starts at belief 0.4 in log-odds. The next question is the unasked atom nearest 0.5, with a bonus for graph centrality and, after a first correct answer, for prerequisite count. A confident correct answer adds 1.55 and floors every prerequisite at +1.4; a slow correct adds 0.55 and nudges prerequisites by 0.55*0.62; a miss subtracts 1.35 and caps every dependent at -1.4. It stops at 18 questions or when no unasked atom sits between 0.32 and 0.68; atoms at or above 0.62 are placed as known.

cited_works.title: A practical perspective on KST: ALEKS and its data
Remark 13.4.5, as reported in JMP2021 section 1.3
cited_works.venue: book, title not given at the citing line

measured_by: placement_done records branch, question count and known count. Per-question answers and the per-atom beliefs are not stored, and no held-out question checks the placement.
verification: doc-and-code-disagree: ADAPTIVE-SOTA.md a.3 specifies a probability distribution over knowledge states, weights near 35 for correct, 5 for incorrect and 50 for an 'I haven't learned this' button, typed answers and a cap near 25; the code keeps one log-odds value per atom with its own weights, a self-judged 'I knew it', and a cap of 18. docs/RESEARCH-OS-APP.md matches the code.
notes: ADAPTIVE-SOTA.md a.2 names the validation to copy from ALEKS: held-out AUROC and a boundary bucket near 0.5. Neither is computed.

name: Seeding known atoms after placement
rule: Each atom placed as known and not yet started is graded once with rating 2 (Hard) at the level its mastery selects, so it enters the review schedule with a short first interval.
measured_by: Seeded cards look like studied cards in state; nothing marks them as inferred.

name: Ten-item assessment
rule: A run takes started atoms (or all askable atoms), due ones first then by leverage, cycles levels recall, apply, derive, teach, and asks 10 items. A correct item is graded rating 3 and a miss rating 1 into the same engine state practice uses. The summary reports score by level, weak atoms and a trust label: high when every item was auto-graded, self when none was, mixed otherwise.
measured_by: assess_done records atomId, level, correct and autoGraded per item, capped at 50 items and 30 events a day. Latency is measured in the client and left out of the event.
verification: doc-and-code-disagree: ADAPTIVE-SOTA.md c.3 and EPIC.md require a sealed checkpoint of fresh items the learner has never seen, kept apart from practice; the run draws from the same atom.quiz items used in study and writes to the same state. LAUNCH-PLAN.md calls it a sealed ten-item assessment.

name: Deterministic answer grader
rule: If the canonical answer holds a number, the last number after the final '=' in each side is compared within 1 percent relative or 1e-9 absolute, and units must match when both give one. A canonical answer of 24 characters or fewer is compared as a normalised string. Anything else is not auto-gradable and falls to self-judgement.
measured_by: autoGraded flag per item in assess_done.
verification: doc-and-code-disagree: ADAPTIVE-SOTA.md c.2 specifies SymPy symbolic equivalence; the code compares normalised strings and one salient number.

name: XP weighted by depth
rule: Any rating above 1 adds XP by level: recall 5, apply 8, derive 14, teach 20.

parameters.name: DEPTH_XP
parameters.source: DECISIONS.md decision 20 sets the direction (XP is mastery-weighted, derive far above recall); the numbers have no stated source

measured_by: Total xp per branch in state.

name: Daily streak
rule: The first graded item of a local day adds 1 to the streak when the previous study day was yesterday and resets it to 1 otherwise.
measured_by: Streak count and last study day in state.
verification: doc-and-code-disagree: DECISIONS.md decision 20 and UX-CASE-STUDIES.md section 13 say streaks are soft and freezable with a free, generous freeze; the code has no freeze.

name: Confidence band on the record
rule: A branch is established at 12 or more mastered atoms and 40 or more reps on cards reviewed in the last 90 days, developing at 4 mastered and 12 total reps, emerging otherwise. The static app bands each concept instead: established at 6 attempts and retention 0.7, developing at 2 attempts and 0.4.
measured_by: nothing
notes: The two code paths band different units with different numbers.

name: Grip sphere
rule: Each canon branch is one axis. Current is the mean mastery of its atoms; peak is the mean of max(mastery, proficiency) per atom. Grip is the unweighted mean of the branch means, shown beside an atom-weighted mean.
measured_by: nothing

formal.theorem: BucketMath.Learning.squared_extent_monotone, coverage_monotone (generic monotonicity; no binding to grip-sphere.ts found)

notes: The UI text says the gap between peak and current is what review brings back; that claim is untested.

name: Lesson at three depths
rule: An atom carries a summary, a lesson and depth texts labelled eli5, core and deep. The tutor prompt labels them PLAIN, CORE and DEEP.
measured_by: nothing
notes: UX-GAP-ANALYSIS.md judged the reading-first default the weakest study mode.

name: Grounded hint-only tutor
rule: The tutor answers from one atom's stored text, up to 12,000 characters, with the last 8 turns of history. The system prompt requires: answer from the grounding alone, abstain when the question falls outside it, give one hint or one guiding question and never the final answer, cite only strings from the atom's own source list, state confidence as high, medium or low, and keep to a few sentences. The server drops any citation absent from the allow-list.

parameters.name: hint-only rule
parameters.value: one hint or one question per turn
parameters.source: Bastani et al. 2025, PNAS, cited in the system prompt and in LITERATURE-REVIEW.md

internal_sources.line_or_heading: Hint-only tutoring is the one design rule with harm data

cited_works.title: Generative AI Without Guardrails Can Harm Learning

measured_by: tutor_turn records atom, abstained, leakBlocked, input and output tokens and cost. The question, the reply and any later quiz result on that atom are not linked.
verification: doc-and-code-disagree: DECISIONS.md Convergence 3 requires retrieval with abstain on weak retrieval and a CI eval rig with a misconception set; the handler grounds on the one atom the client names and I found no eval rig in the files read.
notes: LITERATURE-REVIEW.md gives the evidence: unrestricted GPT-4 raised practice scores 48% and lowered no-AI exam scores 17%; a hint-only tutor showed no exam harm.

name: Answer-leak guard on tutor replies
rule: Each reply is checked against every quiz answer of the atom. It leaks when it contains an answer equation, a number from the answer that the learner and prompt did not supply, or two adjacent sentences holding at least 70 percent of the answer's key words (all of them when the answer has fewer than four). A leak triggers one rewrite; a second leak returns a fixed withheld message.

parameters.name: word-overlap threshold
parameters.value: 0.7 for 4 or more key words, 1.0 below

cited_works.title: Generative AI Without Guardrails Can Harm Learning

measured_by: leakBlocked flag per tutor_turn when both drafts leak. A first-draft leak that the rewrite fixes is not counted. False refusals are not measured.
notes: RESEARCH-PROGRAM-PLAN.md states the hypothesis that a code-level guard cuts answer leaks under adversarial prompts; I found no result for it.

name: Learning event log
rule: Five event names exist. The client may send placement_done, study_session_done and assess_done, each with a daily cap; the server writes tutor_turn. Events are stored only for a profile in the 18plus band that has given learn_event consent, and each carries an optional arm label.
measured_by: This is the web app's whole outcome record: session totals and per-item assessment verdicts. It holds no per-review timestamps, no intervals and no response times.
notes: The arm field allows an experiment split; I found no code that assigns arms in the files read.

name: Three-choice quiz from deck answers
rule: A quiz question shows the item's answer with two distractors drawn from other atoms' answers, same branch first, shuffled by a seeded generator. The time limit is 0.6 seconds per word of prompt plus answer, between 20 and 90 seconds.

internal_sources.line_or_heading: Hint-only tutoring section, retrieval practice paragraph

measured_by: bkt local: attempts table (item_id, mode, encrypted response, correct, rating, elapsed_ms, at) and an outbox row per attempt (packages/bkt/src/store.ts lines 95-99, 363-374).
verification: doc-and-code-disagree: LITERATURE-REVIEW.md says every atom quiz should ask for a generated answer, citing Roediger and Karpicke 2006 and Rowland 2014; this quiz is recognition among three options. Distractors are other atoms' answers; ADAPTIVE-SOTA.md c.1 asks for distractors from student-error models.

name: Rating from correctness and speed
rule: A wrong, missing or late answer rates 1. A correct answer rates 4 when given in under 40 percent of the limit and 3 otherwise. Late means past the limit plus a grace period.
measured_by: elapsed_ms and rating per attempt in attempts and work_quiz_attempts.
notes: The two graders use different grace periods. Rating 2 is never produced by a timed quiz.

name: Self-rated review
rule: Review shows up to 50 due cards one at a time. The learner reveals the answer and picks Again, Hard, Good or Easy, which is sent as rating 1 to 4.
measured_by: Attempt row with mode review, rating and elapsed_ms; correct is stored as rating > 1.
notes: The web Drill uses the same four ratings with the hint 'had it, slowly' for Hard.

name: Quiz session picker
rule: A session takes due items then new items, mapped to each atom's first short-form item. Order: scheduled short items, random short items, scheduled long items from decks with fewer than 20 short items, other scheduled long items, random long items.
measured_by: nothing
notes: New items come in id order here; the prerequisite unlock rule of route() is not applied.

name: Short stem and short answer per item
rule: An item may carry a short stem and short answer written by a rule or a model. A short question needs two distractors whose length matches the answer and that do not appear in the stem, and must pass the length limits; otherwise the long form is used. Its limit is 1.5 seconds per token, between 20 and 45 seconds.
measured_by: nothing

name: Question length limits
rule: A choice question may have a stem of 15 tokens, exactly 3 options of 5 tokens each, a why line of 20 tokens, 30 tokens on screen before answering, and one source link. Options may differ by 1 token and 30 percent in characters. A due card over the limits is rewritten shorter or retired.
measured_by: Count of rewritten and retired cards per request; nothing on whether shorter questions change recall.

name: Question forms
rule: Thirteen forms exist: recall, cloze, true_false, estimate, compare, order, which_changed, cause_effect, spot_error and four language forms (meaning, sound, language, pair). Each pairs with an answer format (pick, word, number, order) and one of three depths. true_false is blocked because a choice question takes three options; which_changed is blocked for lack of a daily snapshot.

parameters.name: form time limits (s)
parameters.value: recall 30, cloze 30, true_false 20, estimate 40, compare 25, order 40, which_changed 25, cause_effect 35, spot_error 45, meaning 20, sound 25, language 15, pair 25

measured_by: work_quiz_coverage counts picks and misses per form/format/depth cell and fact.

name: Coverage-balanced sampler over the learner's own work
rule: Questions come from the learner's beads, pull requests and notes. A daily quiz first takes up to 2 overdue review cards, then walks the form cells from least picked to most, builds up to 16 candidates per cell, and picks one with weight 1 + 2*misses + days overdue per fact. No fact repeats within a quiz or a day.
measured_by: work_quiz_coverage (cell, fact, picks, misses, last_day) and work_quiz_attempts (response, correct, timed_out, skipped, elapsed_ms, rating, mode).

name: Review card created on a miss
rule: A work-quiz question gets an FSRS card only when it is first missed; a first-time correct answer creates no card. Existing cards are rescheduled by the rating.
measured_by: work_quiz_cards holds the card and due date; attempts hold each answer.
notes: Facts answered right once are never scheduled again.

name: Order-of-magnitude grading for estimates
rule: An estimate is right when |log10(got) - log10(want)| is at or under 0.5, and rates 4 at or under 0.15, else 3. The log distance is stored.

parameters.name: FERMI_LOG10_TOLERANCE
parameters.source: packages/bkt/README.md line 145 states the rule (half an order of magnitude); no paper cited

measured_by: log10_distance per attempt in the bkt work_quiz_attempts table.
verification: doc-and-code-disagree: docs/ARCHITECTURE-TARGET.md line 255 records that LOG10_EPSILON accepts pairs just past the boundary, such as 8658 and 27379, which the Lean specification rejects.

name: Surprise quiz during work
rule: While the learner is active on a work page, each active minute past 90 since the last quiz has a 1 in 60 chance of opening one question, at most 2 a day, never while typing. Activity means the tab is visible with input in the last 2 minutes.
measured_by: Attempt mode 'surprise' on each work_quiz_attempts row; skips are stored.

name: Daily quiz
rule: One sealed quiz per day of 3 to 5 questions. Each question is graded once. The writer builds template questions from two days of chat-session stubs and, when a local model answers, puts model-written three-choice recall questions first.
measured_by: work_quiz_attempts row keyed daily:<day>:<question>, with correct, rating, elapsed_ms and log10_distance.

name: Learn-this link after a miss
rule: After a wrong answer the result shows one link labelled 'learn this'. It resolves from the question's first source: an atom to its Academy lesson, an excerpt to its evidence anchor, a work to its DOI, PubMed, arXiv or OpenAlex page. With no such source it links the atom whose title shares at least 2 key terms and more than half its terms with the question text.

parameters.name: title share
parameters.value: more than half of the atom title's key terms

measured_by: nothing; link clicks are not recorded and no later attempt is tied to a followed link.

name: Language lesson loop in the static app
rule: A lesson rotates picture choice, word bank, typed answer, match, listen and phrase exercises. A correct answer grades the word 3 (or the exercise's rating); a miss grades 1, costs one of 5 daily hearts and re-queues the exercise at the end. Onboarding asks target language, reason, a self-rated level that skips 0, 1, 3 or 6 units, and a daily goal of 1, 3, 5 or 8 lessons.

name: Knowledge-space assessment
rule: A 20 to 25 question adaptive assessment keeps a probability distribution over feasible knowledge states and asks the item that halves it; typed answers and an 'I haven't learned this' button limit guessing.

name: Outer fringe as ready-to-learn set
